steps.text: A realistic sculpted lizard is outside what I can build, because my tools can't model free-curving organic forms. The closest versions I can make are below.

args.title: Lizard version
args.question: Which version should I build? Sizes come after you pick one.

choices.label: Flat lizard outline, chain of links
Stacked box segments with a tail

dims.label: Joint clearance
dims.note: Gap so segments swing without fusing

args.part: Articulated lizard chain (flat, print in place)
assumptions: Chain lies flat on the bed; joints swing about vertical pins, so side-to-side motion is in the bed plane.
Each segment is a rounded block with a knuckle at each end, 0.4 mm clearance per joint.
Flat print needs no supports, all overhangs are in the bed plane.
Outline is a stylized flat lizard silhouette, not a sculpted body, because sculpted organic forms are out of tool scope.
Sizes are defaults as you asked; the segment count, length, width and pin are guesses.
questions: Should the four legs be flat plates added to segments 2, 4, 6 and 8?

steps.text:
I built the start of the chain, but it isn't a finished lizard yet, and I haven't sent anything to the printer.

The version you asked for can't be a sculpted lizard, since my tools can't model free-curving organic forms. You didn't pick one of the offered versions, so I went with your "common sizes and sensible defaults" note: a flat chain of 9 segments, 14 mm long, 12 mm wide and 5 mm thick, at a 14.4 mm pitch, so about 129 mm long. The sizes are my guesses except the 150 mm total length you gave, and the chain lies flat so the joints swing side to side and nothing needs supports.

What's there now is nine separate blocks in the design "Articulated lizard chain". The knuckle joints, head, tail and legs are not built yet, so the blocks won't hinge and the total length is short of 150 mm. The next step is to design the joints properly. Should I keep going with a flat stylized silhouette (head, tail and four legs added to the chain), or would you rather a plain segmented chain with no legs?
